answer: Each identity anchors to one IFMGA mountain-guide licence: the register lists one licence per guide, earned after 3 years of training, exams in rock, ice and ski, with a logbook of hut-stamped ascents. No second claim on one licence is allowed, and it lapses without yearly ascents. Each fake costs one real guide: 2,400 units plus 1,095 days, so 100 fakes cost 240,000 units and 300 guide-years, a signal no farm can fake cheaply. Cheapest cheat is hiring a guide for 1,500 units, but that guide surrenders its own licence, and a forged logbook fails the hut-stamp and pigment waymark checks.
